4448.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʷinumi, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷey- (“to pay”). Cognate with ποινή (poinḗ), Sanskrit चयते (cáyate) and Avestan 𐬗𐬌𐬐𐬀𐬫𐬀𐬝 (cikayat̰).

4423.t: From συν- (sŭn-, “together”) + χύσις (khŭ́sĭs, “pouring”), or from συγχέω (sŭnkhéō, “to pour together, confound, trouble”) + -σις (-sĭs).

4430.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dʰegʷʰ- (“to burn”). The unaspirated first consonant is due to Grassmann's law.

4444.t: From Proto-Indo-European *tr-ey-gʷ-, from Proto-Indo-European *terh₁- (“to rub”). Cognate with Latin tero.

4450.t: Uncertain. The sense “penis” likely developed from a more concrete sense, and has been compared to βαλλία (ballĭ́ā, “private parts”) and the ethnonym Τριβαλλοί (Trĭbălloí).

4462.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pʰā́mā, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeh₂-meh₂, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeh₂- (“to speak”). By surface analysis, a full-grade deverbal of φημί (phēmĭ́, “to say; to explain; to argue”).

4452.t: According to Beekes, from a Proto-Indo-European *dʰgʷʰen-, albeit with no certain adduced cognates.

4464.t: From a case form of Proto-Indo-European *dʰéǵʰōm (“earth”) (whence also χθών (khthṓn, “earth”)), traditionally taken as a dative.

4429.t: The suffix -ιγγ- implies a Pre-Greek origin because of non-native pronunciation.

4470.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʰrṓwmə, and related to χρώς (khrṓs, “surface of the body, skin (color)”); see there for more.

4469.t: Nominal formation from the root of χράομαι (khráomai), χρεώ (khreṓ, “to need”), and χρή (khrḗ, “have to, ought”); see the latter for more.

4480.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *né Proto-Indo-European *n̥- Proto-Hellenic *ə- Ancient Greek ἀ- (a-)? Proto-Indo-European *demh₂-der.

4442.t: Perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *trewH-p-, a p-extension of a putative *trewH- (“to rub”), and cognate with τρύω (trúō, “to wear down”) and Proto-Slavic *tryti (“to rub”).

4401.t: From στέγω (stégō, “to cover”) + -η (-ē, action noun suffix).

4463.t: Per Rix (LIV), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰeh₂-n (“to yawn, to gape”) with inchoative suffix -σκω (-skō).

4476.t: From a root *ἀγαν- (*agan-) of uncertain origin plus a suffix -ακτέω (-aktéō, expressive formation suffix), as seen also in ὑλακτέω (hŭlaktéō, “to bark”).

4477.t: From a suffixed derivative of Proto-Indo-European *h₂enk- (“to curve, bend”), whence also ἄγκος (ánkos, “bend”), ἀγκύλος (ankúlos, “curved, bent”).

4481.t: From ἀ- (ă-, “un-”) + θάνατος (thắnătos, “dying”). Sense 4, referring to certain soldiers in Achaemenid Persia, has an uncertain origin.

4485.t: Disputed. Commonly held to be formed from ἄκρος (ákros, “sharp”) and another element of uncertain provenance, e.g. εἴβω (eíbō, “to drop, let fall”) according to Schwyzer, though this is rejected by Beekes & van Beek.

4400.t: From Proto-Indo-European *stéh₂mn̥ (“that which stands, stature”). Cognate with Latin stāmen (“warp of a loom; thread hanging from a distaff”).

4472.t: Uncertain but perhaps related to ψάλιον (psálion, “curb chain”) and ψέλιον (psélion, “armlet”). Maybe from Pre-Greek.

4474.t: The word is related to similar words meaning "foxes", like ψειαί (pseiaí), ψίαι (psíai), φοῦαι (phoûai) and φύλλες (phúlles). These variations cannot be all understood in Indo-European terms.

4459.t: From φύω (phúō, “to grow, to be . . . by nature”) + -η (-ē, nominal suffix).

4461.t: From φαίνω (phaínō, “to bring to light, to cause to appear”) + -μα (-ma, nominal suffix) with -σ- from analogy to other -αίνω : -ασμα or from φάσις (phásis).

4434.t: Unknown, related to τέρμινθος (términthos). The form was perhaps influenced by ἐρέβινθος (erébinthos, “chickpea”).

4409.t: From συναναστρέφω (sŭnănăstréphō, “to turn back together, live together”) + -ή (-ḗ).
